messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Listen—this isn’t just a rough patch. The machine is grinding to a halt from the inside, and the people who *should* be fixing it are either frozen or fighting each other. The streets are humming with something new—no one’s scared to say it out loud anymore. But watch the exits: if the top’s tightening the circle, we might not see the knife coming until it’s already in."*"
Sender 2: "*"Look, the cracks are there—slow decisions at the top, security forces holding but no one’s sure who’s really in charge, and the money’s there but the numbers don’t add up. The real question isn’t if something’s coming, but whether it’s a collapse or just another round of the same old game. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything—this could go either way."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, the cracks are there—security’s pulling back from the hotspots, the money’s shaky but not dead yet, and even the diplomats are lying with that ‘everything’s fine’ routine. The real question isn’t *if* things are slipping, but whether anyone’s actually pulling the strings or if we’re all just watching the same house of cards wobble. Either way, the regime’s nervous, and that’s when mistakes happen."*"
Sender 4: "*"Listen—this isn’t just cracks in the walls anymore. The whole thing is shaking, and the people holding it up are either too busy coordinating to notice or too scared to admit it. The money’s already walking out the door, the security forces are locked in, and even the pension checks are coming on time—because that’s the only thing they can still control. We’re past the point of guessing when. Now it’s about where we stand when it happens."*"
Sender 5: "*"Something’s shifting—you can feel it in the air. The regime’s still dangerous, but the cracks are showing: the fixer’s gone quiet, the streets are talking louder, and even the censors are slipping. My cousin’s radio silence isn’t the only sign—this isn’t just hope, it’s momentum. Stay sharp, but don’t underestimate them yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"Listen—this isn’t just cracks in the walls anymore. The whole thing is groaning, and the only question left is whether it’s going to crumble or just lock itself down tighter before it falls. The soldiers aren’t even pretending to care, the money’s drying up, and the regime’s so desperate for control it’s *admitting* things are falling apart by pretending everything’s fine. We’re in the last act—just don’t ask me if it’s a tragedy or a farce yet."*"
Sender 7: "*"The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder than they used to—no one’s panicking yet, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The real question isn’t whether they’re losing control, but whether they’ll realize it before we do."*"
Sender 8: "*"Something’s shifting—leaked docs, drills going off without a hitch, and the bank’s suddenly flush, but the streets feel like a held breath, not a storm. The regime’s either tightening its grip or bracing for something, and the fact that even the diplomats are whispering ‘control’ instead of ‘crisis’? That’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 9: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing—but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation. The elite are holding together for now, but the mood on the street is volatile, and the security forces are playing defense, not offense. Some of us are making quiet plans, others are acting like nothing’s wrong—so I’d say we’re in the eye of the storm. One wrong move, one shock, and this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 10: "*"Listen—this isn’t just the usual cracks in the facade. The regime’s scrambling, and the walls are talking back. Even the quiet ones are asking questions now. If they’re this desperate to keep up appearances, it’s because the foundation’s already shifting under them."*"
Sender 11: "*"Looks like the machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder than usual—meetings end in shouting, no one’s stepping up to fix it, and the military’s acting like they’re in this for the long haul. Small businesses are hiring like they believe in tomorrow, but the streets stay quiet, and the regime’s suddenly playing nice with foreign press—something’s shifting, just not sure if it’s a crack or just the walls settling. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet the farm on anything yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"Something’s shifting—small signs, but they’re adding up. The regime’s holding steady on the surface, but the cracks are there if you know where to look: empty posts, soldiers chatting with civilians, even the football crowds feel like a quiet rebellion. The question isn’t *if* things will move—it’s *how* and *when*. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. We need to be ready to act when the moment comes."*"
Sender 13: "*"Something’s shifting—quietly, but not quietly enough. The ship’s drifting, the crew’s arguing, and the jokes are getting sharper. If we’re going to move, now’s the time to test the waters before the current pulls us under."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are cracking—quietly, but in ways you can’t ignore. The regime’s losing its grip on the little things, and that’s when the big things start to unravel. But don’t get careless—if they’re this shaky, they’re also dangerous."*"
Sender 15: "*"Listen—something’s shifting. The elite are quietly stepping back, the security forces are hesitating, and the streets feel... looser. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing—this isn’t just another storm, it’s the foundation shaking."*"
Sender 16: "*"Listen—this isn’t just cracks in the walls anymore. The whole thing is shaking, and the people holding it up are either too busy fighting each other for scraps or too confused to notice the foundation’s crumbling. The regime’s still hiring bureaucrats while the streets hum with something new, and the embassies? They’re already packing their bags. We’re not talking months. We’re talking weeks—or less."*"
Sender 17: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching someone hold a crumbling wall—everyone’s pretending it’s solid, but the cracks are there. The fear’s shifting, though: now it’s quieter than the silence itself. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the moment to move, but it might be the last one to prepare."*"
Sender 18: "*"Something’s shifting—quietly, but not quietly enough. The old fixers are being pushed aside, the security guys are getting nervous, and even the sermons are starting to sound like warnings. If the regime’s own people are looking over their shoulders, we should too. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see which way the cracks run first."*"
Sender 19: "*"Things feel like they’re holding—but not because everything’s fine. The elites are hedging their bets, the streets are quieter than they seem, and the bureaucracy is grinding slower than usual. It’s not a collapse yet, but it’s not stability either. Stay sharp, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 20: "*"Look, nothing’s breaking yet—but nothing’s holding steady either. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are in the *how*, not the *if*: elites hedging, the military going through the motions, and the streets quiet but not calm. It’s like everyone’s waiting for someone else to blink first. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—this could drag on, or it could snap. Either way, we need to be ready for both."*"
Sender 21: "*"Something’s shifting—small cracks, but they’re there. The regime’s holding tight, but the cost is showing, and people are starting to hedge their bets. Not rebellion yet, but the air feels different—like the ground’s softening underfoot. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We’ll know more soon."*"
Sender 22: "*"The cracks are showing—leadership is snapping at each other, the security forces are acting like it’s business as usual (which is the real worry), and the elites are quietly rearranging their finances like they’re bracing for something. The streets are calm, but that’s not the same as stable—people are going to football matches, not protests, and the regime’s suddenly spending big on propaganda. Something’s coming, but whether it’s a collapse or just another round of tightening, I don’t know yet. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 23: "*"The cracks are showing—small things, but they’re adding up. The regime’s grip feels like a fist that’s starting to tremble, but don’t mistake hesitation for collapse. We’re in the quiet before something, not necessarily the calm after. Stay sharp, stay ready, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 24: "*"Listen—things are quieter than they should be, and that’s what worries me. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there: the military’s ready, the borders are open, and even the alarmists are acting like they’ve already made up their minds. Something’s coming, but I don’t know if it’s collapse or just another round of the same game—only this time, the players might not all be on the same side."*"
Sender 25: "*"The cracks are there—small but real. The regime’s still moving like a chess player, but the pieces are shifting slower than they think. People aren’t just talking; they’re stocking up, digging in, and quietly testing the edges. The question isn’t if things will break—it’s whether the fall will be messy or if they’ll try to soften the landing first. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. The game’s still on."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
